title: Adult entertainers do not ‘consent to harassment at work,’ EEOC official says
summary: Chicago’s Admiral Theatre in late May settled allegations it allowed customers to engage in unwanted touching of female dancers and subjected Black dancers to different standards and limits.

title: SCOTUS reverse bias decision didn’t nix Title VII comparator requirements, court says
summary: The 5th Circuit rejected a plaintiff’s argument that the high court effectively eliminated his need to show he was treated less favorably than a similarly situated employee.

title: 5 trends shaping skills development
summary: Most HR and IT leaders surveyed said skills improvement is “imperative” within their organizations, CompTIA found.

title: Workers say they turn to AI for advice because it’s less judgmental than colleagues
summary: Although artificial intelligence may be making some employees feel more confident, these tools are also causing a “connection deficit,” Workday said.

title: Do HR practitioners need certifications to thrive professionally?
summary: Probably, veteran HR professionals say. Certifications aren’t the be-all and end-all, but they may give practitioners a competitive edge.

title: Feds confirm overtime-exempt workers can perform nonexempt roles
summary: DOL has addressed overtime calculation issues several times since the relaunch of its opinion letter program in mid-2025.

title: Court partly sides with employer dinged for unlawfully firing workers who shared pay
summary: The NLRB “prejudicially erred” in its decision that a technology firm illegally terminated employees for creating a salary spreadsheet, per the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals.

title: Week in review: How AI will derail careers
summary: We’re rounding up last week’s stories, from the disconnect between front-line workers and leadership to the rise of learning as an HR priority.

title: Wage growth for salaried roles outpaces hourly ones, analysis shows
summary: Even in hourly roles experiencing wage growth, such as in human resources, the gains fell below that seen in salaried roles, Indeed Hiring Lab found.

title: Wells Fargo CEO: AI’s effect on employment is ‘complicated’
summary: The bank’s biggest AI-related challenge is determining how the technology can transform its business model, Charlie Scharf said Wednesday.
